findings.title: A repeated kiosk PIN submit flips the worker's clock state instead of being treated as a retry.
findings.scenario: Omar types his PIN at Tom's kiosk and presses Clock, but the screen lags (or the kiosk resends after a slow network), so the same request arrives twice. The first request clocks him in. The second one sees an open session and clocks him straight back out, leaving a session of almost zero minutes while Omar thinks he is on the clock. The same thing happens at clock-out: a repeated request starts a new session that stays open overnight, so Tom's timesheet shows hours Omar never worked.
findings.test_needed: Send POST kiosk/pin-clock/ twice within 5 seconds with the same PIN and check that exactly one CLOCK_IN exists and the session is still open.

owner_question.question: Omar presses Clock twice within a few seconds at Tom's kiosk. What should happen?
options: The second press within 30 seconds counts as the same action; Omar stays clocked in
The kiosk asks Omar to confirm before clocking out someone who clocked in under a minute ago
Keep today's behaviour: each press flips Omar between clocked in and clocked out
